outline: 48 Rounding Decimals using a Number Line
131 Rounding using the Critical Digit Method

examples.solution_text:
Keep two decimal places: the hundredths digit is $3$.
The next digit is $4$, so keep the $3$.
Remove the digit after the hundredths place.
Rounded value: $22.53$.

Keep one decimal place: the tenths digit is $7$.
The next digit is $9$, so round up.
Increase $7$ to $8$ and remove the hundredths digit.
Rounded value: $246.8$.

Keep one decimal place: the tenths digit is $9$.
The next digit is $8$, so round up.
Increasing $9$ to $10$ carries $1$ into the ones place.
Keep the zero in the tenths place.
Rounded value: $247.0$.

examples.question_text: Round $0.862$ to the nearest whole number.
examples.solution_text:
Cut after the ones digit, $0$.
The critical digit is $8$, so round up.
Increase the ones digit to $1$ and remove the decimal digits.
Rounded value: $1$.

examples.question_text: Write $6.4$ rounded to two decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
There are no further digits to round.
Add a final zero to show two decimal places; the value stays the same.
$6.4 = 6.40$.

Cut after the hundredths digit, $9$.
The critical digit is $8$, so round up.
Increasing the hundredths digit from $9$ to $10$ carries $1$ into the tenths place. This also changes $9$ to $10$, so carry $1$ into the ones place.
Keep two decimal places, including both final zeros.
Rounded value: $8.00$.

Cut after the fourth decimal digit, $9$.
The critical digit is $7$, so round up.
Increasing the fourth decimal digit from $9$ to $10$ carries $1$ through each preceding decimal place into the ones place.
Keep four decimal places, including all four final zeros.
Rounded value: $3.0000$.

methods.description: Cut after the requested place, inspect only the immediately following digit, then keep or increase the rounding digit and remove subsequent digits. Whole-number and decimal-place tasks use this same method.

methods.description: Append or retain final zeros to show the requested number of decimal places without changing the value.
When rounding up changes a retained 9 to 10, carry into the place on its left; repeat through consecutive nines and retain the requested decimal places.

examples.derivation: Cut after the ones place in 0.862. The immediately following digit is 8, so increase 0 to 1 and discard the decimal digits. Answer: 1. This adapts the whole-number rounding tasks at lines 175–178 and 266–279.
6.4 and 6.40 have equal value. Appending one zero expresses two decimal places. Answer: 6.40. The table at lines 340–350 explicitly teaches this precision convention.

The thousandths digit of 7.998 is 8. Rounding up adds 0.01 to the retained 7.99, giving 8.00 through successive carries. Answer: 8.00. This adapts the repeated-carry task and explanation at lines 423–428.

The fifth decimal digit of 2.99997 is 7. Adding 0.0001 to the retained 2.9999 carries through all four decimal places, giving 3.0000. Four-place rounding is supported at lines 390–394, with repeated carrying supported at lines 423–428. This preserves an already accepted assessed method.
